scenario: Sep 3: Al Jazeera reported the heaviest US-Iran exchange in over a month - US strikes on Iran (Sep 1, ~12 killed) drew a multi-front Iranian retaliation on Jordan, Bahrain, Kuwait and Iraq's Erbil (Sep 2), mostly intercepted. Brent eased to $95.45 (-0.19%) and WTI to $90.97 (-0.05%) on Sep 3 (Trading Economics) as the prior spike partially consolidates; TTF is confirmed at 73.36 EUR/MWh (Yahoo Finance, Sep 2), the JKM CFD reference is $23.76 (+0.61%, Trading Economics, Sep 2), and the $22.00 Reuters September-delivery assessment remains carried. QatarEnergy force majeure remains extended into early November. Crisis level remains 4 (High); base 5%, stress 50%, tail 45%.

categories.label: Food & Agriculture
categories.supplyChainImpact: Middle East fertilizer and energy exports remain constrained while Hormuz weekly traffic ticked up to 121 crossings for Aug 17-23, from 118 the prior week, still far below the ~130/day pre-war norm (Foreign Policy Journal/Kpler, Aug 27). Iran and Oman converted the temporary corridor framework into a revenue-sharing arrangement (Al Jazeera, Aug 27), while Iran's transit-fee push and Washington's sanctions pressure sustain freight and input-cost risk for Vietnam, Thailand and Indonesia planting chains; Qatar force majeure remains extended to mid-September.

categories.label: Petrochemicals & Plastics
categories.supplyChainImpact: SABIC, QAPCO and Omani exporters depend on Gulf shipping, while Southeast Asian crackers rely on Gulf condensate and naphtha. Hormuz weekly traffic edged up to 121 crossings for Aug 17-23 (Kpler-sourced, confirmed), while Iran's transit-fee provision and the revenue-sharing corridor agreement with Oman (Al Jazeera, Aug 27) add fresh compliance and routing uncertainty for carriers. Combined feedstock, freight and delivery risk stays elevated for plastics, packaging and agrochemicals.

assets.name: Naphtha (CFR Japan)
assets.narrative: Trading Economics printed the naphtha CFD reference at $745.45/mt on Aug 27 (+0.14% vs the prior close), tracking Brent's steadier tone as corridor diplomacy advanced. A signed reopening would ease Gulf feedstock risk further; a collapsed deal would re-widen it. Source: Trading Economics, confirmed.

assets.name: Methanol (CFR China)
assets.narrative: The latest reviewed methanol observation remains $308/mt from Jul 24. Qatar force majeure and renewed Gulf attacks keep supply and freight risk elevated; no newer approved CFR China assessment is available. Source: Investing.com CFR China, carried.

categories.label: Fertilizers
categories.supplyChainImpact: The Strait of Hormuz remains the critical export artery for Middle East fertilizer supply. Qatar force majeure is extended to mid-September, and Hormuz weekly traffic remains reduced at 121 crossings for Aug 17-23, well below pre-war norms (Kpler-sourced, confirmed). Iran's transit-fee provision and the newly agreed Iran-Oman revenue-sharing corridor framework keep delivery risk elevated across ASEAN planting chains pending a signed reopening.

Source: DTN/Argus Fertilizers, carried.

assets.name: Potash (MOP CFR SE Asia)
assets.narrative: The latest reviewed potash observation remains $418/mt from Jul 24. Renewed attacks and constrained Gulf traffic keep freight and insurance costs uncertain for ASEAN plantation inputs. Source: Argus Fertilizers/CRU, carried.

categories.label: Shipping & Freight
categories.supplyChainImpact: P&I war-risk constraints continue to divert or delay Gulf shipping as Iran's transit-fee requirement meets the newly agreed Iran-Oman revenue-sharing corridor framework (Al Jazeera, Aug 27); CENTCOM said mines were cleared from shipping lanes and about 1,500 vessels have been assisted since the blockade resumed in mid-July (Fox News, Aug 27). Reviewed Kpler data show weekly transits at 121 for Aug 17-23. Current route-normalised VLCC and LNG freight observations remain unavailable, so no verified cost uplift is published.

assets.name: Baltic Dry Index
assets.narrative: The latest reviewed BDI observation is 3,107 points from Aug 27 (Trading Economics), up 1.67% and marking a sixth consecutive session of gains to its highest level since June 3. It measures broad dry-bulk conditions and does not provide a route-normalised Hormuz freight cost. Source: Trading Economics, confirmed.

assets.name: VLCC AG-Asia Rate
assets.narrative: The displayed WS105 level remains an estimate from Jul 24. It is not used in the commercial evaluation because no current route-normalised TD3C observation is approved. Renewed attacks near Khasab and the prospect of a reopening keep the direction of risk two-sided. Source: Seatrade Maritime/Clarkson estimate.

assets.name: Container Freight (SCFI)
assets.narrative: The latest reviewed SCFI observation remains 1,480 points from Jul 24. It is a weekly container benchmark and does not establish current Gulf war-risk or rerouting costs. Source: Shanghai Shipping Exchange, carried.
